title: the breath again — every claim checked
hook: breath gets asked to carry cures, hacks and hidden energies; this stretch checks every claim against the page

segments.voice: Last week closed on sleep: a temple's bedtime and its dawn song, and Rama woken with words.

A sticky note on a bathroom mirror says: just breathe. Fair enough. But breath gets asked to carry a lot more these days. One trick to fix your sleep. One pattern to melt stress away. An ancient secret energy, now in an app. Some of it may help. Some is said with more confidence than the evidence has earned. These last days of the Ayurveda lens come back to the breath, with a promise in the title. Today, the breath again, every claim checked.
screen: `JUST BREATHE.` → `A TRICK, A PATTERN, A SECRET.` → `EVERY CLAIM CHECKED.`

segments.voice: First, the rule for these days. Every claim about breath gets one of three labels. The text says: a line you can find on the page, with a reference. Tradition says: what teachers and families pass down, honored, but not the same as the page. A doctor decides: anything about illness, cure or treatment. This path won't promise a cure. Now one claim, checked. The Yoga Sutras of Patanjali, in the second chapter, describe the breath in practice. Paraphrased: its movement out, its movement in, and its pause, when watched by place, by time and by number, becomes long and fine. The Sanskrit for that last pair is dirgha sukshma, long and subtle. What kind of claim is that? Not a promise about blood pressure or sleep. It describes what happens to breath under attention, and it hands over the method: notice where the breath is felt, how long it lasts, how many there are. Anyone can check it, gently, by watching. Label: the text says, and the watching is yours. Now what the sutra doesn't say. It doesn't say breathe in a special pattern to heal. It offers no number of seconds. Those come from other texts and other teachers, and when they come up, they'll get their own labels. One plain safety line, because breath work isn't neutral. Anyone with a heart or lung condition, anyone pregnant, anyone who gets dizzy or anxious with breath exercises, keeps to easy natural breathing and asks a doctor before any holding of the breath. Today's practice holds nothing. It only watches.
screen: `THREE LABELS FOR EVERY CLAIM` · `WATCHED BY PLACE, TIME AND NUMBER` · `DIRGHA SUKSHMA: LONG AND FINE` · `WHAT THE SUTRA DOESN'T SAY`

segments.voice: Let the breath do whatever it's doing, and check it by place, where it's felt most, then by time, whether the in-breath runs longer than the out-breath, then by number, counting a few breaths from one to five, without changing anything. If it grows longer and finer on its own, notice that; if it doesn't, that's an honest result too. If you pray, let the breath be your prayer.
The breath again. In the Yoga Sutras, breath watched by place, time and number becomes long and fine: a claim you can check by watching. Today's word.
Your line: the breath again — every claim checked. The text says, tradition says, a doctor decides. That's today, done.
